title: Mirrors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W14-2#t1 term and clue written for the game; W14-2#t4 term and clue written for the game; W14-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; W14-2#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W14-2#N.4, W14-2#N.8, W14-2#N.9, W14-2#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mirror equation
items.clue: Relation 1/s_i + 1/s_o = 1/f linking the object and image distances to f.

items.label: Real image
items.clue: Has positive s_i, lies in front of the reflecting surface and is inverted.

items.label: Magnification
items.clue: Ratio |h_i/h_o| = |s_i/s_o|: above 1 means enlarged, below 1 means reduced.

items.label: Convex mirror
items.clue: Has negative f; its reflected rays always diverge, so the result is always virtual, upright and reduced.

questions.stem: A convex mirror in a store shows images of customers standing at various distances in front of it. How does the height of each customer's image compare with the customer's height?

options.text: It is larger, as a convex mirror magnifies, like a magnifying glass.
It is smaller, whatever the customer's distance from the mirror.
It is equal, as a mirror forms images the same size as objects.
It is larger for near customers, smaller for those far away.

questions.stem: An object is placed 30.0 cm in front of a convex mirror whose focal length has a magnitude of 20.0 cm. Use the convention that s_o is positive, s_i is positive for an image in front of the mirror and negative for an image behind it, and f is positive for a concave mirror and negative for a convex mirror. What is the image distance s_i?
An object 2.0 cm tall is placed 15.0 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10.0 cm. What is the height of the image?

A small object is placed on the principal axis of a concave mirror whose radius of curvature is R. The mirror forms an upright image five times as tall as the object. Use the convention that s_o is positive, s_i is positive for an image in front of the mirror and negative for an image behind it, and f is positive for a concave mirror and negative for a convex mirror. Which expression gives the distance of the object from the mirror?
